title: Andaman Islands vs Maldives: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: For adventurers seeking authentic experiences, pristine nature, and incredible value, the Andaman Islands are an undisputed winner, with daily budgets often under $70-$100 USD. If your dream involves unparalleled luxury, overwater bungalows, and a curated, pristine island escape, the Maldives is you

categories.name: h2 id="cost-of-travel">💰 Cost of Travel
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer an incredible travel experience at a fraction of the cost of the Maldives, making it accessible to a much wider range of budgets.

categories.name: h2 id="beaches-scenery">🏖️ Beaches & Scenery
categories.summary: The Maldives offers a consistent, iconic, and meticulously maintained 'paradise' beach experience that is globally unmatched.

categories.name: h2 id="activities-excursions">🐠 Activities & Excursions
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands provide a richer variety of activities spanning adventure, history, and nature, beyond just water sports.

categories.name: h2 id="accommodation">🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: The Maldives offers an unparalleled range of luxury accommodations, particularly the iconic overwater bungalows, which are a destination in themselves.

categories.name: h2 id="food-dining">🍽️ Food & Dining
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer a more authentic, diverse, and significantly more affordable culinary journey centered around fresh seafood and local flavors.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-there">✈️ Getting There
categories.summary: Both destinations have similar travel times from major international hubs, though the internal connections and costs differ significantly after the initial flight.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-around">🚗 Getting Around
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands offer significantly more freedom and affordable options for independent exploration within and between islands.

categories.name: h2 id="culture-local-experience">🎭 Culture & Local Experience
categories.summary: The Andaman Islands provide a vibrant, accessible, and diverse cultural experience, including historical sites and local interactions, which is largely absent in the resort-focused Maldives.

categories.name: h2 id="nightlife-relaxation">🌙 Nightlife & Relaxation
categories.summary: The Maldives excels at providing luxurious, private, and sophisticated relaxation options and resort-based entertainment, perfect for unwinding.

categories.name: h2 id="best-time-to-visit">☀️ Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: Both destinations share a similar optimal travel window (roughly October/December to April/May) due to regional monsoon patterns, offering pleasant weather for tourism.

faq.question: Which destination is better for a honeymoon?
faq.answer: For an extravagant, private, and romantic honeymoon with iconic overwater bungalows and impeccable service, the Maldives is the undisputed choice. However, if you're a couple seeking adventure, cultural immersion, and incredible value, the Andaman Islands offer a unique and memorable romantic getaway without breaking the bank.

faq.question: Are the Andaman Islands safe for solo female travelers?
faq.answer: Yes, the Andaman Islands are generally considered very safe for solo female travelers, especially in tourist areas like Port Blair, Havelock, and Neil Island. Locals are helpful, and crime rates are low. As always, exercise standard precautions, especially at night, but many solo female travelers report positive experiences.

faq.question: What are the visa requirements for each destination?
faq.answer: For the Andaman Islands, foreign nationals generally require an Indian visa. Many countries are eligible for an e-Visa. For the Maldives, most nationalities receive a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they have a valid passport, onward ticket, and sufficient funds. Always check the latest requirements for your nationality.

faq.question: Can I find vegetarian/vegan food easily in both places?
faq.answer: In the Andaman Islands, finding vegetarian and vegan food is very easy due to India's strong vegetarian culinary tradition. Most local restaurants and cafes offer numerous options. In the Maldives, resorts cater to international diets and can accommodate dietary restrictions, but local island cuisine might be more limited in vegan options; vegetarian is generally available.

faq.question: Which destination has better snorkeling and diving?
faq.answer: Both offer world-class snorkeling and diving with vibrant coral reefs and abundant marine life. The Maldives often has more easily accessible house reefs directly from resorts. The Andaman Islands, particularly around Havelock and Neil Island, boast incredible, less crowded dive sites and often offer more affordable diving certifications.

faq.question: What's the wildlife like in each place?
faq.answer: The Andaman Islands offer a rich blend of marine and terrestrial wildlife, including diverse bird species, wild elephants (on some islands), and saltwater crocodiles (caution advised). The Maldives is primarily known for its stunning marine life: sharks, rays, turtles, and countless reef fish, with very little terrestrial wildlife beyond birds and lizards.

faq.question: Is alcohol allowed in both destinations?
faq.answer: In the Andaman Islands, alcohol is freely available at licensed shops, bars, and restaurants. In the Maldives, alcohol is strictly prohibited on local islands due to Islamic law, but it is freely served within all private resort islands and liveaboards. Be mindful of local customs when visiting non-resort areas in the Maldives.

faq.question: What are the major airports for each destination?
faq.answer: The main airport for the Andaman Islands is Veer Savarkar International Airport (IXZ) in Port Blair, requiring a connecting domestic flight within India. For the Maldives, the primary international gateway is Velana International Airport (MLE) in Malé, which receives direct flights from numerous global cities.
